messages:
joel: dropping a quick prototype of 'cost-sleuth' — an interactive per-invocation breakdown you can click into from the cost dashboard. focuses: token-level cost, cache crediting, and model-version attribution. PR: https://git/repo/pulls/789 :sparkles:
anya: Love the name. How lightweight is the per-invocation payload? worried about kafka churn if we emit full traces for every request
joel: It's a summary record only. schema v0.2: `inv_id, timestamp, effective_model, tokens_in/out, cache_flags, prefetch_flag, node_cost_components, model_version_tag` (all compact). full trace is available on-demand via lookup id, not in the stream
rachel: For cache crediting, are we doing a first-touch or last-touch allocation? both camps show up in finance meetings
joel: Default is first-touch (where KV hit occurred). But the UI has a toggle: allocation_method = [first-touch | proportional | amortized] and the waterfall recomputes client-side from sampled econ rows
anya: If UI recomputes, we need deterministic algorithms so CSV exports match backend billing. Could be a nightmare otherwise
joel: Good point. We'll publish the exact algorithm in the API spec and add a backend flag to freeze computation for exports (`freeze_allocation=true`) so finance exports use backend-determined values
ops-bot: infra: cost-sleuth-staging deploy started at 2026-03-21T15:30Z
pm-ash: UX ask: add a tiny inline estimator that shows "if you changed route X to prefer model Y what would be the delta" without running a full canary
joel: Added a lightweight estimator: it runs a single-pass fold over sampled records and returns delta estimate + sample CI. It's intentionally fast ~200ms for 1k samples
anya: How are we treating reserved capacity? Our unit costs for some tenants drop dramatically when covered by Dedicated capacity commitments
joel: There's a tenancy-cost-layer. We join econ records with commitment coverage table at query-time. You can switch cost basis to "blended" or "hosted-only". Also exposes per-token amortized GPU op cost field
rachel: Privacy: model_version_tag sometimes contains internal build hashes. We need to strip or map for customer-facing exports
joel: We emit `model_hash` and a human-friendly `model_label`. Exports and public UI will only show `model_label`. Internal support pages require RBAC to view the mapping
ops-bot: infra: deploy completed to staging :white_check_mark:
anya: Rollouts: would be awesome if the dashboard could schedule a routing policy flip for a window and auto-generate a reconciliation report at window close
joel: Scheduler added. You can schedule `routing_policy_change(route, start, end, pct)` and it will compile a post-run reconciliation that compares allocated vs actual cache credits and cost impact
pm-ash: Add auto-alert if reconciliation shows >5% discrepancy vs projected. finance will want a notification channel
joel: Yep hookable to Slack channels and email. also added an "explain" mode that shows the top 5 sample invocations driving any discrepancy
rachel: Sampling detail: show sample_rate and the exact seed used so results are reproducible for audit
joel: Done. `sample_rate` shown and `sample_seed` baked into the export. Also an explainability toggle to surface representative prompt fingerprints (no raw content)
anya: For on-call: can we have a cheap heatmap tile showing "hot routes by cache-value" so SREs can quickly spot cache regressions
joel: There's a tiny tile that ranks routes by estimated cache-dollar-value lost (based on recent delta). designed to be lightweight and refresh every minute
ops-bot: alert-monitor: simulated canary run flagged latency regression on candidate model at 3/21 15:42; auto-revert executed
pm-ash: Documentation: add a short section about assumptions for the estimator and the reconciliation algorithm. PMs will cite it in runbooks
joel: Will add docs + example CSV schema. I'll also attach a sample reconciliation report to the PR
anya: One more: exports for auditors should include model quantization tag and runtime kernel id (helps for billing and performance tuning)
joel: Added `quant_tag` and `kernel_id` to econ summary. They are included only in internal exports; masked in customer-facing files
rachel: Awesome. When you push screenshots to #eng-platform we'll sanity-check numbers against tenant samples
joel: Will do in 10m. tagging @anya @rachel @pm-ash. thanks all
